To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

maternal immune activation (a model of maternal infection during pregnancy) causes gastrointestinal abnormalities in the offspring and that these abnormalities are associated with behavioral abnormalities.
maternal immune activation (an animal model of autism) causes gut barrier defects, gut microbial dysbiosis, and behavioral abnormalities in the offspring.

maternal immune activation in mice causes behavioral and physiological abnormalities that resemble features of neurodevelopmental disorders and that treatment with a human commensal bacterial species ameliorates these abnormalities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the gut microbiome in the pathophysiology of ASD.
the role of the microbiota in the development of neurodevelopmental disorders and the potential for probiotics as a therapy.
the role of the gut microbiome in the development of ASD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gut microbiome is a key player in the development of the brain and that gut microbiota dysbiosis can lead to behavioral and physiological changes that are associated with autism and other neurodevelopmental disorders.
this paper demonstrates that the gut microbiome can modulate the behavioral, physiological and metabolic abnormalities associated with neurodevelopmental disorders in mice.
the gut microbiota can be manipulated to ameliorate behavioral and physiological abnormalities associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the maternal immune activation model of neurodevelopmental disorder has gut microbiota and gut permeability abnormalities, and we have shown that these abnormalities can be corrected by the probiotic Bacteroides.

we have shown that the gut microbiota can be manipulated by the administration of a probiotic (Bacteroides fragils) to reverse behavioral and physiological abnormalities associated with a mouse model of neurodevelopmental disorders (maternal immune activation).
the gut-brain axis can be a therapeutic target for neurodevelopmental disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gut microbiota may be involved in the pathophysiology of autism and other neurodevelopmental disorders, and that probiotics may provide a therapeutic approach to treating these disorders.
gut bacteria are important for brain development.
gut bacteria may be an effective treatment for behavioral and GI symptoms in ASD.
